clue.text: Open-and-shut, possibly, according to circumstances?

definitions.meaning: an open-and-shut case is one kind a case may be, so the phrase describes a case that might be that
a stock phrase meaning depending on how things turn out

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is cryptic: 'Open-and-shut' is one way a case may be, with 'possibly' hinting at the may.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning whichever applies in the particular situation.

clue.text: With the whole of 8's repertoire, etc …

definitions.meaning: 8-down is the jazz trumpeter, so all of his repertoire is everything plus the jazz
a colloquial tag meaning and everything else of that kind

explanation.walkthrough: The '8' points to 8-down, the famous jazz trumpeter; the phrase is also a casual way of saying 'and so on'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is a dismissive way of ending a list, the same job as et cetera.

clue.text: … conducting exam is stressful

definitions.meaning: setting someone an examination is putting them to the test
a trying, demanding experience is described with this adjective

explanation.surface: Running an examination puts the invigilator under strain.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to 1-down in the surface only; it plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A testing time is a hard, stressful one, and conducting an exam is examining or trying out.

clue.text: English knight laid into lout climbing tree

indicators.note: the knight is set inside the other piece, as if laid into it
in a down clue, climbing means the word is read upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: a yob is a lout or hooligan
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: An English knight attacks a hooligan who is up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns YOB into BOY, and 'laid into' puts N inside that to give BONY, after E.
explanation.definitionFit: This tropical hardwood tree yields the very dark timber of the same name.

clue.text: Stirred, as well as mincing?

definitions.meaning: walking or speaking in an artificial, dainty manner

explanation.walkthrough: 'as well as' is a link between the two senses: moved emotionally, and artificial or pretentious.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both emotionally moved and putting on airs, as a mincing manner does.

clue.text: Catch panther for a change, not horse

indicators.note: the letters are altered in order, signalled by the idea of change
the named letter is left out of the fodder

parts.note: H is slang for heroin, known as horse

explanation.surface: Trap a big cat, as a novelty, rather than a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not horse' removes H (heroin, slang horse) from PANTHER to leave PANTER; 'for a change' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrap someone is to catch them out, usually by a trick.

clue.text: Informing and evaluating in Albert Square?

indicators.note: Albert Square is the setting of the London soap EastEnders, so the word is said in a Cockney accent

parts.note: to appraise is to assess or evaluate

explanation.surface: Gossip and assessments circulating in a famous TV square.
explanation.walkthrough: Albert Square is the East London square of the BBC soap EastEnders; a Cockney says the 'ay' of the evaluating word like 'eye'.
explanation.definitionFit: To apprise someone is to inform them or tell them of something.

clue.text: Players take time dressing

parts.note: a band is a group of musical players
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Musicians take ages getting dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandage is a strip of material used as a dressing for a wound.

clue.text: Trumpeter left our organist confused about manuscript

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the other piece
the letters of the fodder are muddled, signalled by confused

explanation.surface: A trumpet player departs, leaving the church organist baffled by the score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges OUR ORGANIST and 'about' wraps those letters around MS, all after L.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Orleans jazz trumpeter nicknamed Satchmo is the famous example.

clue.text: Throw first of missiles in nightclub attack

indicators.note: the single letter is placed inside the pieces

parts.note: a disco is a nightclub for dancing
a fit is a sudden attack, as of coughing

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: Someone hurls the first projectile in a nightclub brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw' is the definition in the sense of disconcert, not a physical toss.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw someone is to unsettle them, which is what discomfiting them does.

clue.text: Battle the French abandoned for entertainment

indicators.note: the French article is dropped from the battle's name

parts.note: Lepanto was a 1571 naval battle between the Holy League and the Ottomans
le is French for the

explanation.surface: French forces quit the fight to go to a show.
explanation.walkthrough: The Battle of Lepanto (1571) loses LE, French for 'the'. PANTO is the British Christmas pantomime, a family stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantomime is a traditional British comic stage entertainment staged at Christmas.

clue.text: But many of them are engaged in clerical work

definitions.text: But many of them are engaged in clerical work

parts.words: But many of them are engaged in clerical work
parts.note: clerical reads as churchly, yet the people meant are the non-clergy, many of whom do office jobs

explanation.walkthrough: 'clerical' means office work here; the people described are precisely those who are not clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: The laity are the ordinary members of a church, as opposed to the ordained clergy.

clue.text: Hubbub a competitor cut short in assembly of rich

indicators.note: the middle pieces sit inside the rearranged letters
the letters are put together in a new order
the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a rival is a competitor

explanation.surface: A clamour as a rival is interrupted at a gathering of the wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' takes L off RIVAL; A plus RIVA goes 'in' CHRI, made by 'assembly of' RICH.
explanation.definitionFit: A charivari is a noisy mock serenade, hence any din or hubbub.

clue.text: Why Orpheus followed Eurydice to Hades in company?

definitions.text: Why Orpheus followed Eurydice to Hades
definitions.meaning: Orpheus went down to the underworld in order to fetch his wife back, read as three words

explanation.walkthrough: Read as three words, the answer says why Orpheus went to Hades: to fetch his wife back.
explanation.definitionFit: Together means in one another's company, side by side.

clue.text: Sailor-boy wearing sailor's hat

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
Paul is a boy's name
dressed in something is wearing it

explanation.surface: A young seaman dons a naval cap.
explanation.walkthrough: A tarpaulin was once a sailor's tarred hat (and a sailor), not just a waterproof sheet.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a tarpaulin was a broad-brimmed tarred hat worn by seamen.

clue.text: US agency keeping back people's pictures

indicators.note: the agency holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency

indicators.note: the word is read in reverse

parts.note: men is a word for people

explanation.surface: An American intelligence service is withholding citizens' photographs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'people's' looks like a possessive of 'pictures', but the 's is only a link; 'pictures' is the old British phrase for films.
explanation.definitionFit: Going to the pictures is an old British expression for going to the cinema.

clue.text: Latest directions supporting Norwegian play

indicators.note: in a down clue, the piece that supports another sits beneath it

parts.note: Brand is an 1865 verse drama by the Norwegian Henrik Ibsen
N, E and W are compass directions

explanation.surface: New stage directions underpin a Scandinavian drama.
explanation.walkthrough: Brand is a play by Ibsen; the compass points N, E, W sit below it in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something brand-new is the very latest, fresh and unused.

clue.text: Agreement — one that Sullivan lost, say?

indicators.note: the word is spoken, so a phrase that sounds the same is wanted

parts.note: Arthur Sullivan wrote the song The Lost Chord, so what he lost was a chord

explanation.surface: An agreement that a composer famously mislaid.
explanation.walkthrough: Sullivan (of Gilbert and Sullivan) wrote the Victorian song 'The Lost Chord'.
explanation.definitionFit: An accord is an agreement or harmony between parties.

clue.text: Bill's companion's tirade interrupting dance

indicators.note: the outburst breaks into the middle of the other word

parts.note: in the phrase bill and coo, the companion of bill is coo
a rant is a tirade

explanation.surface: A friend of Bill launches into a rant during the dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' is not a man's name here but the bill of 'bill and coo', the lovebirds' phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The coranto, or courante, is an old running dance in triple time.

clue.text: Herb's beginning to invest in medieval music

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the music

parts.note: organum is an early form of polyphony from the Middle Ages

indicators.note: only the start of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: Herbal start-up putting money into early music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herb's' is 'herb is', the 's a link to the wordplay. Organum is medieval part-singing.
explanation.definitionFit: Origanum is the genus of herbs that includes oregano and marjoram.

clue.text: Reportedly mischievous untruth regarding molluscs

indicators.note: the word is heard, so a phrase sounding alike is meant

parts.note: a naughty lie is a mischievous untruth

explanation.surface: Gossip spreads a cheeky fib about shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautili are cephalopod sea creatures with spiral chambered shells, a kind of mollusc.

clue.text: "Her indoors" appears to regret our absence

definitions.meaning: a jokey British phrase for one's wife
to feel sorry that we are not there is to pine for us

explanation.walkthrough: 'Her indoors' is British slang for a wife; split in two, the answer also means feeling the lack of us.
explanation.definitionFit: Missus is informal for wife, the same person jokingly called her indoors.

clue.text: Asian river crossed by girl and two boys

indicators.note: the river letter is spanned by the names around it

parts.note: Jo is a girl's name
Dan is one boy's name
Ian is the other boy's name

explanation.surface: A girl and two lads are ferried across an Asian river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Asian river' suggests the Jordan itself, but 'Asian' alone is the definition and the river is just the abbreviation R.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jordanian is a person from Jordan, a country in western Asia.

clue.text: Bleak place associated with Edward III's son

definitions.text: place associated with Edward III's son
definitions.meaning: John of ..., son of Edward III, was named after Ghent, his birthplace

explanation.walkthrough: John of Gaunt was named after Ghent, then called Gaunt in English.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaunt landscape is bleak and desolate, and Gaunt is the old English name for Ghent.

clue.text: Whig PM missing on shoot

indicators.note: the named word is absent from the name

parts.note: the Duke of Grafton was a Whig prime minister in the 1760s

explanation.surface: A prime minister skips a shooting party.
explanation.definitionFit: A graft is a shoot or scion inserted into another plant.

clue.text: Like area featuring in quiz on Alberta

indicators.note: the letters are found running through the words that follow

explanation.surface: A Canadian province appears in a trivia contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Zonal means relating to a zone, and a zone is an area.

clue.text: Damage in sickbay in old European state

parts.note: san, short for sanatorium, is a school sickbay
to mar is to damage

explanation.surface: Harm suffered in a school infirmary in an old country.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'European state'; 'old' supplies the final O, though it reads as describing the state.
explanation.definitionFit: San Marino is an ancient tiny republic in Europe, surrounded by Italy.

clue.text: Exmoor outlaw's object after broadcast -— behave naturally

indicators.note: the object's word comes after the broadcast one

parts.note: the Doones were the outlaw clan of Exmoor in R. D. Blackmore's novel Lorna Doone
sown means scattered, like seed broadcast by hand
a thing is an object

explanation.surface: A West Country bandit's possession is publicised; he acts as he pleases.
explanation.walkthrough: Exmoor is moorland in south-west England; 'broadcast' means scattered seed, not radio.
explanation.definitionFit: To do one's own thing is an idiom for acting as one wishes, independently and naturally.
